title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Logcat that survives a device switch, and a Run that asks
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.27 fixes the Logcat panel and Android Run: a device switch that left the panel empty, an unplugged phone that respawned adb every two seconds and then replayed its whole buffer, accents turned into replacement characters, a secondary process hijacking the PID filter, a Run that picked the emulator over the phone without asking, and a build command Windows could not run.

highlights.title: Logcat follows the device
highlights.description: Switching devices keeps the app filter working, an unplugged phone stops the stream instead of respawning adb, and its return resumes after the last row rather than replaying the whole buffer.

highlights.title: Rows read as the device wrote them
highlights.description: UTF-8 split across chunks, buffer markers glued to messages, mangled Kotlin and R8 frames, and an export in UTC are all fixed; the scroll position holds while the buffer evicts.

highlights.title: Run picks the right device
highlights.description: A picker appears when several devices are connected, the build command works in PowerShell and cmd.exe, and a disabled launcher alias no longer wins over the real activity.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A device switch re-resolves the followed PID; a secondary `:sync` process is followed alongside the main one instead of replacing it.
An unplugged device shows a stream error, stops the retries, and resumes with `-T` after the last buffered row when it comes back.
UTF-8 sequences split across stdout chunks, `--------- beginning of` markers, `toString-impl` and `SourceFile` frames, `UtilsKt` top-level functions and the export timestamp are handled.
Reading back through a full buffer no longer scrolls under your eyes, and adb installed mid-session is found without a reload.
Run asks which device when several are connected, quotes nothing PowerShell rejects, and skips disabled launcher aliases.
